card.statement:
Let $\mathscr{C}$ and $\omega$ be as in Proposition 2.2. Set

$B:=\varinjlim_{X}B_{X}.$

Then $\omega$ admits a canonical factorization

$\textstyle{\mathscr{C}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\scriptstyle{\overline{\omega}}$ $\scriptstyle{\omega}$ $\textstyle{{\mathop{\mathrm{Comod}}}_{B}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\scriptstyle{{\mathord{\mathrm{forget}}}}$ $\textstyle{{\mathord{\mathrm{Vect}}}_{\mathbf{k}}}$

where $\overline{\omega}$ is an equivalence of categories.

Here, the fact that $\omega(X)$ admits a structure of $B$ -comodule (for $X$ in $\mathscr{C}$ ) means that there exists a canonical morphism $\omega(X)\to\omega(X)\otimes_{\mathbf{k}}B$ satisfying the appropriate axioms. In other words, we have obtained a canonical morphism of functors $\omega\to\omega\otimes_{\mathbf{k}}B$, where the right-hand side means the functor $X\mapsto\omega(X)\otimes_{\mathbf{k}}B$ (and where we omit the natural functor from ${\mathord{\mathrm{Vect}}}_{\mathbf{k}}$ to the category of all $\mathbf{k}$ -vector spaces).
card.label: Theorem 2.4

paper.title: Notes on the geometric Satake equivalence
paper.abstract: These notes are devoted to a detailed exposition of the proof of the Geometric Satake Equivalence for general coefficients, following Mirkovic-Vilonen.
